title: DNS & DHCP
description: How names resolve and how hosts get their addresses.

questions.prompt: What does a DNS A record map?
choices: A hostname to an IPv4 address
An IP address to a hostname
A domain to its mail server
questions.explanation: A records map a name to an IPv4 address. AAAA is the IPv6 equivalent, CNAME aliases a name, PTR is reverse lookup and MX names mail servers.

questions.prompt: Which DNS record type makes one name an alias of another name?
questions.explanation: A CNAME says 'this name is really that name'. Resolvers then look up the target name instead.

questions.prompt: A recursive resolver has nothing cached for www.example.com. Which servers does it ask, in order?
questions.explanation: The resolver starts at a root server, which refers it to the .com TLD servers, which refer it to example.com's authoritative servers, which return the answer.

questions.prompt: Which of these are real DNS record types? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: MX (mail exchanger) and NS (name server) are DNS records. ARP and SMTP are protocols, not record types.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the DHCP exchange?
questions.explanation: Often remembered as DORA: the client Discovers, a server Offers, the client Requests the offer, and the server Acknowledges.

questions.prompt: Which transport and port does a normal DNS query use?
questions.explanation: Standard queries use UDP port 53. DNS falls back to TCP 53 for large responses and zone transfers. UDP 67/68 is DHCP.

questions.prompt: Why does a DHCP client send its Discover message as a broadcast?
choices: It has no IP address yet and does not know the server's address
DHCP servers only listen for broadcasts on port 80
questions.explanation: The client has no address (it sends from 0.0.0.0) and doesn't know where a DHCP server is, so it broadcasts to 255.255.255.255 on the local link.

questions.prompt: You are migrating a site to a new IP and the old DNS record had a TTL of 24 hours. What is the main risk?
choices: The new server will reject requests
Some clients keep resolving the old IP until their cache expires
questions.explanation: Resolvers may cache the old answer for up to the TTL. A common practice is to lower the TTL well before a migration and raise it again afterwards.
